key_insight: Diffusion-based reconstruction can flag fatal cerebral hemorrhage on postmortem CT, and adding weak image-level labels markedly improves anomaly detection.
clinical_relevance: This could support faster forensic triage of brain PMCT by helping prioritize scans with suspected fatal intracranial hemorrhage.
method: Retrospective PMCT study of 265 healthy cases and 33 fatal intracranial hemorrhage cases from a single forensic institute.
Automated brain extraction, slice selection, and intensity normalization prepared the scans for modeling.
Compared an unsupervised AnoDDPM trained on healthy anatomy with a weakly supervised classifier-guided diffusion model using image-level death-cause labels.
evidence_signal: At the image level, AnoDDPM achieved AUROC 0.928 and AUPRC 0.794, while the classifier-guided model achieved AUROC 0.991 and AUPRC 0.960, each with bootstrap confidence intervals.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data with limited hemorrhage cases may restrict generalizability and the method still needs external validation before routine use.
paper_title: 2D anomaly detection of fatal cerebral hemorrhage on postmortem CT
